tour.overview:
On 24 August of the year 79 – or in October, as new evidence suggests – Mount Vesuvius blew apart and buried the Roman town of Pompeii under several metres of ash and pumice. The town lay hidden for more than 1,600 years. Since excavations began in 1748, archaeologists have uncovered two-thirds of it: streets rutted by cart wheels, shops with their counters, bakeries with their ovens, frescoed villas and an amphitheatre older than the Colosseum. Pompeii, Herculaneum and Torre Annunziata have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997.

This private day pairs the most famous archaeological site in the world with the volcano that destroyed it. In the morning, your licensed guide takes you through Pompeii's forum, baths, theatres and the best of its painted houses, avoiding the crowded main streets. After a lunch of local dishes and Vesuvius wine at a family winery, your driver takes you up the mountain to the national park trail, where you walk to the crater rim and look down into the volcano and out over the whole Bay of Naples.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours 30 minutes
• Start and end: your hotel in Naples or Sorrento, or the cruise port of Naples
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; about 5 km in Pompeii on uneven Roman paving, then a 30-minute climb to the crater on a gravel path

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Forum, the Basilica and the Temple of Apollo.
• The Stabian Baths and the Large and Small Theatres.
• A Roman bakery, a thermopolium (street-food counter) and the House of the Faun.
• The plaster casts of victims of the eruption.
• The crater of Mount Vesuvius.
• Panoramas over the Bay of Naples.

WHY THIS WORKS
We start in Pompeii at opening time, before the heat and the cruise groups, and go up Vesuvius in the afternoon, when most visitors have left the trail.

WHO IT SUITS
Anyone curious about daily life in Roman times, families with older children and walkers who want to stand on a live volcano.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer coastal scenery and villages, choose our Amalfi Coast day tour. If walking on uneven ground is difficult, we can replace Vesuvius with Herculaneum, which is smaller and flatter.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
There is almost no shade in Pompeii: bring a hat, sun cream and water in summer. Sturdy shoes are essential for the crater path. The Vesuvius trail closes in strong wind, heavy rain or fire risk; we then visit Herculaneum instead.

days.name: Pompeii with a licensed guide, lunch at a Vesuvius winery and the crater of Mount Vesuvius
days.description:
What to expect: the Roman town buried in 79 and the volcano that buried it, with a licensed guide, private car, tickets and lunch.

Your driver collects you at your hotel in Naples or Sorrento, or at the cruise terminal, at about 8:00, and drives you along the bay to Pompeii in about 40 minutes. Your guide meets you at the gate at opening time. You enter through the Porta Marina and walk up to the Forum, the civic heart of the town, with the Basilica where justice was done, the Temple of Apollo and the cone of Vesuvius rising behind the Temple of Jupiter – the same view the Pompeians had every morning.

You follow streets where the stepping stones and the grooves of cart wheels are still in place. You go inside the Stabian Baths, with their changing rooms and stucco vaults, see a bakery with its millstones and oven, and a thermopolium, a counter where Romans bought hot food. You visit the House of the Faun, the largest private house in town, and other villas with painted walls in the famous Pompeian red. You see the Large and Small Theatres and, in a quiet corner, the plaster casts made from the hollows the victims left in the ash, a moving reminder of the human side of the disaster. Depending on the day, your guide includes recently restored houses and the newest excavations open to visitors.

At about 13:00 your driver takes you to a family winery on the slopes of Vesuvius for lunch: pizza or pasta, local cheeses and vegetables grown in the volcanic soil, with a tasting of Lacryma Christi wine. In the afternoon you drive up to about 1,000 metres, where the national park trail begins. A gravel path climbs in about 30 minutes to the crater rim, 1,281 metres above the sea. You look down into the crater, 200 metres deep, with its occasional wisps of steam, and out over Naples, Capri and the Sorrento peninsula. You are back at your hotel at about 17:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:00 – Pick-up at your hotel or the cruise port.
09:00 – Guided visit of Pompeii (about 3 hours).
12:30 – Drive to a winery on Vesuvius.
13:00 – Lunch with wine tasting.
14:45 – Drive up to the Vesuvius National Park.
15:15 – Walk to the crater rim and back (about 1 hour 30 minutes).
16:45 – Drive back.
17:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Vesuvius tickets are timed and sold by the national park; we book them for you.
• If the crater trail is closed because of weather, we visit Herculaneum, the smaller sister town, instead.
• Cruise passengers: we adapt the day so you are back at the ship at least one hour before all-aboard time.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide in Pompeii, tickets to Pompeii and the Vesuvius trail, lunch with wine tasting, bottled water, pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: guide on the Vesuvius trail (park guides explain at the top), extra drinks, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Can we do this tour from Rome?
faq.answer: Yes. From Rome it is a long day of about 12 hours, with roughly 2 hours 30 minutes each way by car, or we can meet you at Naples station off the high-speed train. Ask us and we will quote the version that suits you.

faq.question: How difficult is the walk up Vesuvius?
faq.answer: The path is about 2 km each way with a steady climb of some 150 metres on loose gravel. Most reasonably fit people manage it in about 30 minutes up. It is not suitable for people with heart or breathing problems.

faq.question: What happens if the Vesuvius trail is closed?
faq.answer: The national park closes the trail in strong wind, heavy rain or fire risk. We then visit the ruins of Herculaneum, which are smaller but even better preserved, with wooden beams and upper floors.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: Pompeii and the Vesuvius crater trail. Your guide in Pompeii is licensed by the region of Campania.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, lunch at a family winery on the slopes of Vesuvius with a tasting of their wines. Non-alcoholic drinks and vegetarian or other diets are no problem.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, for children who can walk a few kilometres. They love the bakeries, the graffiti on the walls and standing on a volcano. We shorten the visit for younger children.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Pompeii has an accessible route on smooth paths to some areas, but most streets have big stepping stones and uneven paving, and the crater path is steep. Tell us your needs and we will adapt the day.

faq.question: Can you pick us up from the cruise ship?
faq.answer: Yes. We meet you at the cruise terminal in Naples and plan the day so you are back at least one hour before the ship's all-aboard time.

faq.question: Will we be taken to cameo or coral shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops. If you want to see a cameo workshop in Torre del Greco, just ask.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Sturdy closed shoes with grip, a hat and sun protection. Bring a light jacket, because it is often cool and windy at the crater, even in summer.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to June and September to October. July and August are very hot in Pompeii; winter is quiet but the crater can be cloudy or closed by bad weather.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
